 WisDOT: Steps to obtain an ID to use at the polls
 Nick Witwer Updated 2026년 11월 2일 월 오후 12:19 UTC 0 (WFRV) - The Wisconsin Department of Transportation Division of Motor Vehicles is explaining the required steps of how to obtain an ID to show at the polls on Election Day.
 According to a release from WisDOT, Wisconsin residents are required to show identification in order to cast their ballot; however, there is no separate 'voter ID' currently required, and a federally compliant 'REAL ID' is also not required in order to vote in the Badger State.
 Voters who are US citizens can check the Wisconsin Elections Commission website to discover what forms of ID are accepted at the polls.

 Those who do not already have some form of approved ID, such as a Wisconsin driver's license, should start by bringing the required documents and applying for their Wisconsin ID at the nearest DMV . Scheduling an appointment at the DMV is said to be available, but not required.
 Officials say there is a process available to US citizens that is free of charge in order to obtain a receipt valid to take to the polls on election day should their ID card not be available in time.
 Additional questions on obtaining an ID can be answered via the DMV's toll-free hotline at (844) 588-1069. Questions about voter eligibility, poll locations, voter registration information, or other election information can be answered via the Wisconsin Elections Commission website .
